$schema.description: Editor hint pointing at this meta-schema. Ignored by the loader.

oneOf.description: Legacy flat map: { <listKey>: <uiSpec> }. Kept so third-party packs still validate.

allOf.$comment: `path` is required for every kind EXCEPT `group`. A group binds no storage at all -- it is a heading with nested sections under it, restoring the two-level structure the hand-written editors had (preferences' "Code Style" over its three lists, lifestyle's "Wellness" over sleep/energy/stress). Giving it a path would be noise that every renderer must then remember not to read.
A group carries no storage-binding key, so declaring one is a sign the node was meant to be a list or fields node. Rejected rather than ignored.

Two rules that apply to list nodes only. (1) `entity`: a list node binds editable controls to an entity's stored keys, so it must name that entity. Without it the renderer still renders (falling back to node-level field_defaults/enum/optional) but tests/test_ui_schema.py has no entity to check the field names against, and a control bound to a key nothing stores would ship unnoticed. (2) a non-empty `path`: an empty path addresses the containing object itself, and writes go through setAt, where `path.length === 0` returns the new value -- so the first write to a list node with `path: []` REPLACES what contains it. Top level that discards the section's whole stored object; on a child list it replaces the parent row's item, losing its id, its title and every other field. Array.isArray([]) is true, so no renderer-side guard can catch it. This is conditional on kind rather than a blanket minItems on `path` because kind: "fields" legitimately uses `path: []` to address the section root (profile's top-level scalars) -- see tests/test_ui_schema.py::test_fields_node_with_empty_path_is_accepted.

$comment.description: Authoring note about this node, carried in the manifest because JSON has no comment syntax. Ignored by the loader and by every renderer. Use it for a fact a later author must not rediscover the hard way -- e.g. a legacy storage key the node deliberately does not bind. NOT user-facing: `info` is what the UI shows.

description.description: One muted line under the node's title, saying what belongs here. User-facing helper text, unlike `$comment` (an authoring note) and shorter than `info` (a dialog). Optional: a node whose title is self-explanatory should omit it rather than restate itself.

item_control.description: How a `strings` node presents each stored string. "tag" (the default) renders ArrayInput's chips -- right for short, word-like values you add and remove but never revise. "input" renders one editable row per string with its own delete -- right for sentence-like values where a typo means retyping the whole thing, which is how the hand-written editors rendered profile's work and education highlights.

placeholder.description: Placeholder for this node's own input -- the ArrayInput on a `strings` node. Carries the concrete examples the hand-written editors used ("e.g. Python, TypeScript..."), which do more to explain a free-text list than any label. Optional: without it a `strings` node derives a plain "Add <singular title>...".

date_fields.description: Storage keys rendered as a date picker. Values must be yyyy-mm-dd; anything else falls back to a text input so it is not discarded.

bool_fields.description: Storage keys rendered as an on/off switch. For keys genuinely stored as JSON booleans -- preferences.response_format is five of them. A missing key reads as off, and the control always writes a real boolean, never the string "true".

time_fields.description: Storage keys rendered as a time picker -- lifestyle's bedtime/wakeup, which the hand-written editor rendered as <input type="time">. Same rule and same reason as date_fields: values must be HH:MM, and anything else falls back to a text input rather than being silently discarded by a picker that cannot parse it. Nothing validates these on write, so an MCP client can store "after midnight".

field_placeholders.description: Placeholder text per storage key, for the text, textarea, date, time and chip controls a node renders. Keyed by field like `field_defaults`, and distinct from the singular `placeholder`, which belongs to a `strings` node's own one input. Optional: a field with no entry renders an empty control. Concrete examples earn their place here -- "e.g. Bachelor's, Master's, PhD" says more about `degree_level` than its label can.

field_defaults.description: Values preselected on a new item. The exact value "@now" is replaced by an ISO 8601 timestamp at add time; every other value is used literally.

sections.description: Nodes nested under a `group` heading. Recursive, like `children` -- but unlike `children`, a nested section's `path` resolves against the SECTION ROOT, not against a row's item: a group is a visual container, not a data scope.

children.description: Nodes rendered inside an expanded list row. A child's `path` resolves against the ROW'S ITEM, not the section root -- e.g. `["references"]` on a list of projects addresses `project.references`. Children are full uiSection nodes (this $ref is recursive), so a child list must name its own `entity` like any other list node.

pinned.description: Lifts the ONE row holding `field` out of the list and renders it above, as the section's answer to a question the list cannot answer -- "which of these is your design language". The lifted row is excluded from the list below rather than shown twice, `field` never renders as an editable control or appears in the Add dialog, and every other row gets a star to claim the slot. Pair it with the entity's `exclusive_fields` so both writers keep it to one.

noun.description: What the slot is called in a control's accessible name, e.g. "primary" -> "Make Brutalist primary".

sort.description: Display order only. Rows are sorted by this storage key; the stored array is never reordered. Two numbers compare numerically; everything else compares as text. Items where the key is missing or an empty string sort last, regardless of direction.

searchable.description: Renders a search box filtering rows on the title field, badges, detail fields and array-field entries.

facets.description: Storage keys with enum values, rendered as a filter above the list. Display only; never writes.

info.description: Content for the section's info dialog.

display_fields.description: Storage keys shown read-only as badges on the collapsed row. Unlike `badges`, these are never rendered as editable controls -- use for machine-written values such as a created-at stamp.

count_badges.description: Array-valued storage keys shown read-only as "N <field>" chips on the collapsed row (e.g. "3 references"), rendered after display_fields and before badges. Never rendered as an editable control. A key that is absent, empty, or not an array on a given item renders no chip for that item -- a "0 x" chip would be noise on every row that has not used the feature.

display_formats.description: Optional per-field formatting for `display_fields`. Values are parsed as dates and rendered in local time; an unparseable value is shown verbatim.

fields_outside_entity.description: Storage keys this node binds that the entity's tool-contract vocabulary (required + optional) deliberately does not carry. Documentation only -- the renderer ignores it. Declaring them here is how a pack whose ui names diverge from its entity names opts that node out of the spelling check in tests/test_ui_schema.py, so the divergence is stated in the manifest instead of the pack being dropped from a test list.

$comment.description: Authoring note about this entity, on the same terms as uiSection's `$comment`: ignored by the loader, never shown to anyone. `description` is the MCP-facing text a client reads in get_schema, so provenance notes -- when a field was added and which follow-up it closed -- belong here, not there.

field_defaults.description: Values preselected on a new item. The exact value "@now" is replaced by an ISO 8601 timestamp at add time; every other value is used literally.

exclusive_fields.description: Storage keys that at most ONE item in this entity's list may hold as true. Setting it on one item clears it on every other, in BOTH writers -- the renderer and execute_modify -- because either alone leaves the invariant enforceable from only one side. `aesthetics.aesthetic.primary` is the case it exists for: the primary entry is what rides into the minimal context scope, and two primaries would make that a coin toss.
